subject: Re: thoughts on the future of perception tooling
text:
Hi [NAME],

I've been following AEye's work on 4Sight, and it's a really impressive
approach to 4D LiDAR perception. Thought I'd reach out as I've recently
been working with teams from Woven by Toyota, Zipline, and Boston Dynamics
to fuse their 2D and 3D ML pipelines in Encord.

As a result, we've been building out LiDAR-specific functionality in close
collaboration with their AI teams, and are now looking to work with others
leading the space like AEye to help shape the next wave of perception
tooling.

Would you be open to a short chat to see the platform and share your
perspective? I'd love to get your candid feedback and compare notes on
where perception data infrastructure is heading.

I'm SF-based and happy to come by next week and give you a demo (Thursday's
open my side) - or we can set up a quick virtual call if easier.

subject: Coffee in Austin - Surgical data accuracy
text:
Hi [NAME],

I wanted to reach out since our leadership team will be in Austin next
week. We work with surgical robotic teams e.g. Moon Sugrical, Kaliber Labs
and Telos Health who, similar to [COMPANY], are building high-precision
systems for operations - it'd be great to connect while we're in town.

For context - we help surgical AI teams improve annotation reliability.
With Encord, they can better orchestrate annotation to QA workflows,
reducing manual labelling times and refocus clinical expert effort on label
quality. We've also built our tool to capture the granularities of surgical
contexts - complex onotology and coordination between modalities (image,
video, DICOM, NiFTI, etc.)

Our leadership team would love to exchange perspectives. They'll be in
Austin Wed (10/19) to Thurs (10/20) next week - would you be open for a
quick coffee?

subject: Large SKU catalogues workaround
text:
Hi [NAME],

We've been working with several retail CV teams (most recently Augmodo) who
run large SKU catalogues and ingest millions of frames a day. The common
pain we're seeing is:

   - slow annotation throughput,
   - inefficient frame-by-frame workflows
   - difficulty connecting catalogue systems to labelling

Most have adopted Encord for two things:

   1. video-native tracking to massively increase frames labelled per action
   2. SDK integration so they can plug in their own models, trigger
   tracking flows, and tie annotations directly to their existing catalogue
   tools (without replacing them)

If you're facing something similar at [COMPANY], happy to share more. I'm free
next Thursday if that works.
